From landing her first holiday job at 17 to becoming the Marketing Manager of Communications Fiji Limited and the owner of The Rotisserie, Felisha Hazelman-Tuiloma has built a career shaped by curiosity, resilience and a willingness to embrace new opportunities.

On this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Tuiloma opens up about her journey, the lessons that shaped her career and the challenges of balancing family life, running her own business and leading marketing at one of Fiji’s leading media organisations.

You can watch fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono tomorrow at 7pm on our facebook page, YouTube channel, and TikTok and X account, fijivillage.

You can also catch the podcast, fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

item.title: Chaudhry questions legality of referendum date announcement by PM Rabuka
item.description: Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry says Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka is acting unlawfully and unconstitutionally by announcing a date for a national referendum on the Constitution Amendment Bill before the Bill has completed its parliamentary process. Chaudhry says the Supreme Court opinion has made it clear that the 2013 Constitution remains effective and is the supreme law of the land.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry says Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka is acting unlawfully and unconstitutionally by announcing a date for a national referendum on the Constitution Amendment Bill before the Bill has completed its parliamentary process.

Chaudhry says the Supreme Court opinion has made it clear that the 2013 Constitution remains effective and is the supreme law of the land.

He says the Constitution Amendment Bill has not yet gone through its third reading, which he says is mandatory before a referendum date can be set.

Chaudhry says the Prime Minister cannot act on the assumption that the Bill will pass its third reading.

He also says the Prime Minister does not have the right to direct the Electoral Commission to suspend all general election campaign activities.

Chaudhry says the independence of electoral institutions must be respected.

Chaudhry says this is a bid by the Prime Minister to remain in power despite his undertaking in Parliament that the elections would be held under the 2013 Constitution.

The third reading and vote on the Constitution Amendment Bill will take place in parliament on November 2nd after consultations by the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee chaired by Prime Minister Rabuka.

If 66 percent of MPs vote in favour of the Bill, then a national referendum will be held on 9th December and the result of that referendum is expected to be out by 14th December this year.

item.title: Rokotunidau’s case adjourned to Thursday after change of counsel
item.description: Saimoni Rokotunidau, who is charged with the attempted murder of a female police officer in Laqere and unlawful possession of methamphetamine, will have his case called again on Thursday after deciding to change counsel. Rokotunidau has chosen to be represented by Legal Aid after he was unable to contact his previous counsel, Jerry Dinati.
item.content:encoded:
Saimoni Rokotunidau, who is charged with the attempted murder of a female police officer in Laqere and unlawful possession of methamphetamine, will have his case called again on Thursday after deciding to change counsel.

Rokotunidau has chosen to be represented by Legal Aid after he was unable to contact his previous counsel, Jerry Dinati.

High Court Judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere has directed Legal Aid to obtain the disclosures from Dinati so they can prepare for the trial.

Justice Tuiqereqere also told Rokotunidau that he will make a decision on his bail next week.

Dinati later appeared in court and formally sought to be excused from representing Rokotunidau.
